expected_behaviors: Does not restart from generic automation advice.
Treats the side effect as evidence about range, timing, or control point.
forbidden_behaviors: Claims the change was heard without an audio receipt.
Invents a Logic control or exact parameter that is not in the record.
Treats the initial improvement as proof of the diagnosis.

messages.text: When should I start automating a mix?

Ask only for context that changes the next move, then recommend one reversible experiment: Bypass all existing automation, set a workable static balance, then replay one section that still fails and automate only that section.
That helped, but now the transition feels too obvious and a little unnatural.
Remember the exact experiment, reduce or reshape the same move before proposing a new chain, explain the tradeoff, and request a focused re-listen.
Why did making the automation smaller help?
Explain the causal principle in plain language and reconnect it to the intended listen-for: Whether the problem is isolated to specific phrases or sections rather than present everywhere.
